skills.description: Finds sources against your brief, summarises the parts that actually relate to your assignment, then writes the in-text citations and reference list in the style you are required to use — all three in one pass, so you get something to hand in, not a pile of links. Built to save students the hours spent finding and reading sources, not to write the paper for them
skills.description_zh:
Assignment Literature Assistant: **it is not a search tool that hands you a pile of
links.** Give it your assignment brief (plus your slides, handouts, course page or a
screenshot of the brief) and it does three things in one pass:
① **finds real sources against what your brief actually asks for**;
② **summarises only the parts that relate to your assignment** — not a generic abstract
of each paper, and every line points back to a section and a sentence in the source;
③ **writes the in-text citations and a formatted reference list in the exact style your
assignment demands**.

You want something you can hand in, not a pile of links. So the output is finished
work: which papers to use, which section and sentence in each one contains the point
you need, **what the parts relevant to your brief say**, what the citation looks like,
how the reference list is laid out. **Every conclusion links back to the source it
came from.**

Every result comes with a link you can click and check yourself, plus a DOI.
**And it checks one thing about every single one: has this paper been retracted by its
publisher?** Retraction is not deletion — the page, the PDF and the link usually all
stay up and the download still works, so **being findable is not the same as being
usable**. Anything found to be retracted is flagged separately, with the retraction
notice link and a plain "not recommended for direct citation".

It locates the thing your brief actually demands
inside the paper: if your assignment requires Gibbs' reflective cycle, a named
instrument, or a specific variable, it goes into the full text and tells you which
section it appears in, quotes the sentence, and gives you the link to verify it.
If the full text cannot be retrieved, it says so **in plain words and tells you which
kind of problem it is** — "this one needs payment, I cannot reach the full text",
"it is listed as open access but the download is blocked on my side". No hedging, no
sugar-coating. **What it can summarise, it hands over first**: sources that are
relevant and reachable still get located, summarised, cited and listed. The ones it
could not open are listed afterwards, with how far they got through the relevance
check, a link you can open, and your options — **whether to pay is your call**, it
will not make it for you and will not show you a way around the paywall. **It never
asks for your username or password**, and it will not ask you to log into an account
to fetch a paper for it.

Only then does it write the citation: in-text citations and a formatted reference
list in the **citation style** your assignment demands (APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago, IEEE,
Vancouver, Harvard or GB/T 7714). Every field comes from real retrieved metadata — if
there is no DOI, there is no DOI in your list, and nothing is filled in to make it
look complete. **Every style name comes with a label saying it is a citation style,
plus one line on what it is and which subjects use it** — it never throws a bare
"MLA 9" at you and leaves you to guess. Say Harvard and it warns you: that style has
no official standard version, so it will ask for your school's guide or a sample.

It can read these: a screenshot of the brief, essays and handout files, slide decks,
PDFs (it downloads them and reads the text layer), scanned image-only PDFs (it pulls
the page image out and reads that — measured to work), subtitle or transcript files
(it cannot read audio or video itself — you need subtitles or a transcript), and a
public web page you point it at, which it asks about first.

Digits and proper nouns read from an image are flagged "read from the image, please
check the original" — and if an image is too blurry it says so instead of guessing.

Just talk to it normally, no need to say "literature":
"I have to write a literature review on X, find me some solid sources"
"Find me papers on X, summarise the parts relevant to my question, and write the
citations and reference list in APA 7"
"I don't know where to start looking" "I want to quote this sentence, how do I cite it"
"My reference list is in the wrong format" "Format my references in APA 7"
"Is this journal predatory?" "Is this paper worth citing?"
"This one is paywalled, is there a free version?" "Summarise this lecture transcript".

It will not write your paragraphs for you,
it will not lower your similarity score or AI-detection score, it will not log in
to anything on your behalf, and it will never give you a paraphrase without a source.

Free for now.

skills.description_zh: 小红书单条笔记「提取 + 加工」双段流水线，**免登录、免付费、免换链接**。提取段一条命令出成套素材（标题/作者/时间/正文/标签/全部原图/视频直链 + manifest 完整度）；加工段把长图/截图内容转录成**可追责**的结构化数据（证据分级 A/B、三级 verdict、多源核验、机器校验闸门）。适用于：① 甩来一个小红书链接要"看看里面是什么 / 核对一下"；② 内容全在截图里（题库答案、清单、教程、对比表）；③ 页面被"IP 存在风险 / 错误码 300012"拦截；④ 页面 HTML 里翻不到 noteDetailMap / imageList；⑤ 链接没带 xsec_token 落到了推荐流。触发词：小红书、xiaohongshu、xhslink、笔记链接、把图拉下来、答案都在截图里、IP 存在风险、300012。不适用于：批量爬取他人笔记、未指定链接的关键词搜索（搜索页需登录）、视频大文件下载（用 yt-dlp）、热榜与推荐流采样。
skills.name: 小红书提取与长图结构化

skills.description: 面向幼儿园教师（小/中/大班）的幼儿园环境创设方案助手。基于《指南》"创设丰富教育环境"精神与通用幼教环境理念，提供班级区角、主题墙、自然角、阅读区、户外活动区、心理环境等场景的创设方案（空间规划+材料清单+步骤+安全适配），把"想布置"变成"能落地、安全、适宜"的环境方案。数据自包含、不依赖联网。适用于"帮我设计中班建构区""自然角怎么布置""主题墙方案""阅读角太小怎么弄"等场景。

skills.description: 按企业、国家出资企业、政府采购当事人、事业单位、社会组织五个口径判断是否构成关联方，输出名单与关系说明，并提示同一关系在不同口径下结论不同的情形。
skills.description_zh: 跨域关联方识别。按企业、国家出资企业、政府采购当事人、事业单位、社会组织五个口径判断某一主体是否构成关联方，输出关联方名单与关系说明，并提示同一关系在不同口径下结论不同的情形。当用户问"这算不算关联方""这两家有没有关联关系""投标前要不要回避""年报要报哪些关联方"时使用。
skills.name: 关联方识别（跨域版）
